Recommended Highlights This Week

1. FIFA World Cup 2026 – Round of 16 concludes, Quarterfinals begin

2. The Portals Experience – new immersive exhibition

3. CRYBABY at Resorts World Sentosa – new inflatable sculpture activation

4. Bibim Deli – new DIY Korean rice bowls

5. Sukiyaki Jin – Singapore's first A5 wagyu tomato sukiyaki

6. Downtown Line Friday night early closures begin – from 10 July

Overall Summary

The World Cup narrows further this week as the Round of 16 wraps up and the Quarterfinals begin, with several co-host nations already eliminated – expect fan zone energy to stay high right through the weekend. On Sentosa and at Scotts Road, two new immersive experiences open their doors: CRYBABY's giant inflatable sea creatures at Resorts World Sentosa, and The Portals Experience, a fantasy and sci-fi walkthrough near Orchard. On the transport side, note that Downtown Line Friday night early closures begin this week and will run for several weeks.

Events & Festivals

FIFA World Cup 2026 – Round of 16 & Quarterfinals

The Round of 16 concludes this week with several upsets, including Norway's shock win over five-time champions Brazil, before the Quarterfinals begin on the 9th.

Round of 16 (concludes):

- Mon 6 July: Spain 1-0 Portugal, Dallas – kickoff 3:00am SGT (7 July)

- Mon 6 July: Belgium 4-1 USA, Seattle – kickoff 8:00am SGT (7 July)

- Tue 7 July: Argentina 3-2 Egypt, Atlanta

Quarterfinals begin:

- Thu 9 July: France 2-0 Morocco, Boston

- Fri 10 July: Spain 2-1 Belgium, Los Angeles

- Sat 11 July: England 2-1 Norway (AET), Miami; Argentina 3-1 Switzerland (AET), Kansas City

Location: Lau Pa Sat / CHIJMES / Capitol Singapore (public fan zones)

Concierge Recommendation: Semifinal spots are now on the line – expect the loudest crowds of the tournament so far for the Argentina and England fixtures this weekend.

Attractions & Activities

The Portals Experience

A new fantasy and sci-fi immersive experience opens near Orchard, built around original artworks, themed realms, miniatures and interactive displays.

Event Date: Opens this week, until 2 September 2026

Time: 9:00am–9:00pm, last entry 8:00pm

Location: Fever Exhibition Hall, 25 Scotts Road

Admission: From S$26 for adults and S$17 for children

Website: https://portals-experience.sg/

Recommended Duration: 60–90 minutes

Best For: Families / Sci-Fi Fans / Fantasy Fans / Orchard Area Guests

Concierge Recommendation: A handy new option for guests based near Orchard, especially useful on a rainy afternoon.

CRYBABY at Resorts World Sentosa

Three five-metre inflatable sculptures – an anglerfish, a pufferfish and a whale shark – have gone on display across RWS, alongside a CRYBABY pop-up store near the Coach Singapore boutique.

Event Date: This week, until 30 August 2026

Location: Resorts World Sentosa

Best For: Families / Young Adults / Collectors / Photography

Concierge Recommendation: A fun, free add-on for anyone already spending the day at RWS – great for photos.

Restaurants & Bars

Bibim Deli

Culinary Class Wars season one chef Yohan Kim has opened this economical Korean DIY rice bowl concept, letting diners mix and match more than 20 rotating banchan and sauces onto a free base bowl of rice.

Best For: Solo Diners / Casual Lunch / Korean Cuisine Fans / Budget-Conscious Guests

Concierge Recommendation: A good value lunch recommendation for guests wanting something quick and casual between meetings.

Sukiyaki Jin

Singapore's first A5 wagyu tomato sukiyaki has arrived in Orchard, putting a tomato-based twist on the traditional hot pot.

Location: Orchard

Best For: Couples / Japanese Cuisine Fans / Special Occasions

Concierge Recommendation: A distinctive dinner pick for guests who've already tried the more familiar sukiyaki spots and want something different.

Hotel & Hospitality News

Pan Pacific Hotels Group – Cluster GM Appointment

Pan Pacific Hotels Group has appointed Kung Teong Wah as cluster general manager overseeing both Parkroyal Collection Pickering, Singapore and Parkroyal on Beach Road, Singapore, expanding his existing role at Parkroyal Collection Pickering.

General Manager: Kung Teong Wah – more than three decades of hospitality experience, with deep expertise in Singapore's hotel sector; previously General Manager of Parkroyal on Beach Road

Transport & Operational Updates

Downtown Line Night Works – Begins This Week

From 10 July, trains on the entire Downtown Line end at 11:30pm on Friday nights and resume at 8:30am on Saturdays, continuing over several weeks while systems testing is carried out. Shuttle buses cover the gap.

FIFA Fan Zone Crowds

Quarterfinal weekend (9–11 July) will bring heavier footfall and later closing hours around Lau Pa Sat, CHIJMES and Capitol Singapore.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Mid-year travel season traffic remains high. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

Looking Ahead

FIFA World Cup 2026 – Semifinals

Semifinals are set for 14 and 15 July: France v Spain and England v Argentina. Expect this to be the busiest fan zone weekend of the tournament so far.

Concierge Recommendation: Guests should be advised to book fan zone seating or arrive well ahead of kickoff for the semifinals – these are expected to draw the largest crowds yet.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Downtown Line Friday night early closures begin this week – flag this for any guests with late Friday travel plans via the DTL.

  • CRYBABY and The Portals Experience both make good rainy-day or between-meetings additions for guests already in the RWS or Orchard areas.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day

Sentosa Family Time

A Magical Island Adventure - CRYBABY photo stops - Southernmost Point evening lighting

Full Day

Orchard & Civic District

The Portals Experience - Bibim Deli lunch - Seoul & So dinner at National Gallery

2 Days

Day 1

Gardens by the Bay - Juju World Singapore - Sukiyaki Jin dinner

Day 2

FIFA Quarterfinal fan zone at Lau Pa Sat - ATLAS nightcap
